A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BTR research. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial presentation changes and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Atari, Procgen and Wii-game experiments, component ablations, robustness tests and hardware measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports revised benchmark results, additional comparisons and an Atari-5 regression validation.

M1.justification: The six BTR extensions, network architecture and Munchausen-IQN loss remain unchanged. Layer normalization was already an experimental variant in v1; it is not a newly adopted component. Changed preprocessing and hyperparameters are evaluation-setting revisions.

E1.justification: Atari, Procgen and the three Wii tasks are retained; the additional Atari subset comparisons reuse existing games. However, Mario Kart's completion requirement changes from three laps in v1 Appendix K.2 to four in v2 Appendix J.2, while v2 Figure 4 still shows 'LAP 2/3'. Whether an actually evaluated task requirement changed is unresolved.

E2.justification: V2 adds Rainbow DQN comparisons on the Wii games, PQN in Table A3, PPO+Impala in Figure B4, and broader Atari comparisons including BBF, EfficientZero-v2, C51, REM and DreamerV2. Table A1 replaces the full Rainbow column with DQN, although full Rainbow remains in Table A2. Comparator coverage changes substantially.

E3.justification: Procgen preprocessing changes from four stacked grayscale frames to one color frame, and epsilon decay changes from 2M to 8M frames. V2 adds overlap-based Atari comparisons, optimality-gap reporting and regression-predicted medians. Normalization references also change, including AirRaid's human score from 3000 to 1000 in Table A1. These establish reported protocol revisions without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a Rainbow+vectorization control in Figure C6 and tests Atari-5's predicted median against the full benchmark in Appendix K. The separate neuron-activation histograms from v1 Appendix F disappear. Most existing component, layer-normalization, exploration, sticky-action and life-information analyses remain.

E5.justification: Ablation captions change from three seeds and standard-deviation bands to four seeds and 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals. V2 newly specifies five Procgen seeds and adds confidence intervals for Table 2 in Table E8. Reporting remains inconsistent: Tables 2/E7 specify three seeds, whereas Table E8 specifies six, preventing a clear reconstruction of those runs.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation values change: BTR's Atari-60 IQM becomes 7.361 from 7.419, Atari-5 IQM becomes 7.739 from 7.627, and Table 2 policy churn becomes 3.8% from 2.9%. Wii figures revise first completion from 105M to 150M frames for Super Mario Galaxy and 50M to 77M for Mortal Kombat. Additional comparison results are reported; changed settings and run reporting limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, Q-learning and Munchausen equations, and appendix loss function are mathematically unchanged. The new Atari-5 regression analysis empirically applies an existing procedure; no new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about integrating six improvements, approximately 7.4 Atari-60 IQM, exceeding humans on 52 games and solving three Wii tasks remain. V2 qualifies the under-12-hour training claim as requiring a high-end desktop PC, narrowing its stated resource scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 substantially revises the Impala/plasticity interpretation, including reversing the wording about its effect on dormant neurons, and narrows the noise-robustness explanation to maxpooling. V2 also explicitly acknowledges that BTR is below Procgen state of the art, that Atari-5 regression mispredicts its full-suite median, and that the single-seed sticky-action result warrants caution.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code-repository address to the abstract, identifies the target-update search values as 250, 500 and 1000, and documents implementation backends in the PQN comparison. The architecture, loss, hardware descriptions and detailed Wii setup largely remain available. The Adam-epsilon explanatory fraction is corrected without changing its stated numerical value.

R1.justification: V2 adds relevant citations for statistical evaluation, hyperparameter selection, spectral normalization, newer comparators and Procgen generalization, while removing the Dopamine and Pillow references. The central positioning relative to Fast and Efficient Rainbow and computationally expensive agents remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence largely remain. V2 copyedits wording, expands explanations of exploration and adaptive pooling, reorganizes appendices, converts experimental notes into lists, and replaces the ethics/reproducibility section with an impact statement and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout and extensively redraws and reorganizes displays. Figure 1 changes from frames to A100 walltime; new comparison panels, performance profiles and regression plots appear. Wii plots gain baseline curves, individual ablations move to the appendix, and several plots change normalization, axes and uncertainty displays.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, explicit confidence intervals, a code address and clearer applicability limits improve the transparency and assessability of the empirical claims. However, conflicting seed counts in Tables 2/E8 and Mortal Kombat's 77M-frame completion in Figure 4 versus 50M in Appendix J.3 weaken reporting consistency. These unresolved discrepancies temper the gains, supporting a limited overall improvement.
